slot.brief: Given a balanced combustion equation of a liquid hydrocarbon, compute Δn_g (gaseous moles products minus reactants) and then apply ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g RT for the numeric answer.

stem:
For the combustion of liquid toluene at 298 K:
C7H8(l) + 9O2(g) -> 7CO2(g) + 4H2O(l)
The value of delta H - delta U (in kJ mol^-1) is closest to (take R = 8.314 J K^-1 mol^-1):
working: Gaseous products: 7 mol CO2; gaseous reactants: 9 mol O2. delta n_g = 7 - 9 = -2. delta H = delta U + delta n_g R T, so delta H - delta U = delta n_g R T = -2 * 8.314 * 298 = -4955.144 J mol^-1 = -4.96 kJ mol^-1.
solution:
For gaseous species, $\Delta H-\Delta U=\Delta n_gRT$, where $\Delta n_g=7-9=-2$.
$$\Delta H-\Delta U=(-2)(8.314)(298)=-4955\text{ J mol}^{-1}\approx -4.96\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
